qt: to the Commission Eva Kaili (NI) Subject:

The European Union has made major investments in vaccine research and development (R&D). Such projects seek to achieve two primary goals: first, to speed up the development, production and distribution of vaccines against COVID-19 and other diseases; and secondly, to improve readiness for future pandemics, including research into next-generation vaccines. In this regard: 1.

What can the Commission do to support all those citizens who were obliged to be vaccinated due to the lack of alternative options, and suffered severe consequences, as we recently saw on the news, but are receiving inadequate compensation to cover their needs?

Beyond direct funding, what other forms of financial support (e.g. loan guarantees) have been provided to private and public entities and, in each case, what legal form does this aid take (e.g. advance purchase agreements)?

Has the Commission considered contractual clauses regarding intellectual property rights (IPRs) and exploitation rights for the vaccines it finances and what is its position on ensuring patent rights for these vaccines?
at: (English version) to the Commission Eva Kaili (NI) (25 March 2024) Subject: The EU’s investment in vaccine R&D: funding, support and intellectual property considerations The European Union has made major investments in vaccine research and development (R&D). Such projects seek to achieve two primary goals: first, to speed up the development, production and distribution of vaccines against COVID-19 and other diseases; and secondly, to improve readiness for future pandemics, including research into next-generation vaccines. In this regard: 1.

What can the Commission do to support all those citizens who were obliged to be vaccinated due to the lack of alternative options, and suffered severe consequences, as we recently saw on the news, but are receiving inadequate compensation to cover their needs?

Beyond direct funding, what other forms of financial support (e.g. loan guarantees) have been provided to private and public entities and, in each case, what legal form does this aid take (e.g. advance purchase agreements)?

Has the Commission considered contractual clauses regarding intellectual property rights (IPRs) and exploitation rights for the vaccines it finances and what is its position on ensuring patent rights for these vaccines?

(26 August 2024) As regards suspected side effects of COVID-19 vaccines, the European Medicines Agency and national authorities evaluate data on reported events in EudraVigilance (1) to determine any need to act. The authorised COVID-19 vaccines’ efficacy and safety have been further confirmed by the reassuring data, which was gathered following their use in hundreds of millions of people worldwide. In accordance with the Advance Purchase Agreements (APAs) for the purchase of COVID-19 vaccines, the administration of COVID-19 vaccines was conducted under the sole responsibility of the Member States; there is therefore no formal role for the Commission in proceedings concerning third-party claims. These agreements for COVID-19 vaccines included up-front EU financing to de-risk essential investments in order to increase the speed and scale of manufacturing successful vaccines. The Commission did not acquire intellectual property rights for the secured vaccines. In addition, the Commission provides financial support for vaccine research and development through the Horizon Europe programme (2) (3) as well as the EU4Health programme (4) (5). EU4Health and Horizon Europe-supported research and innovation projects are bound to respect the programmes’ rules on intellectual property rights (6).
